text.p: The following are the reports carried by Estonia's newspapers on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these reports and does not vouch for their accuracy:
- Estonia opened its embassy in Portugal. Meelike Palli, temporary charge d'affaires, heads the embassy.
- Former member of parliament Lo Vooglaid was convicted of causing the death of two women in a traffic accident. He received a four-year suspended sentence.
- The Chamber of Commerce and Industry is critical of the business plan of NRG Energy, the U.S. company intending to buy the Narva power stations.

- The defence, interior, transport and environment minsters discussed on Monday the possibility of merging the ships of the navy, border guard, maritime inspection and maritime board into a single fleet.
- The trial of Eero Kadarik, ex-prefect of Laane-Virumaa county police, began yesterday. He is accused of having used the labour of prisoners while building his home.
- Tallinn city council opposition considers a no confidence vote against chairman Edgar Savisaar unlikely.

- An anonymous expert ruled out the survival of Captain Avo Piht in the disaster of the ferry "Estonia" after ex-chairman of the investigating commission Andi Meister announced the publication of his book, which claims that eight surviving crew members are still missing.
- Narva authorities will wait until the end of the week before deciding whether to cut the water supply to Ivangorod. The Russian town has again failed to pay for water.
- Estonia's advertising market may double this year and reach 600 million kroons.
- Hansatee shipping line is considering the likelihood of operating in the Black Sea on the Odessa-Istanbul line.
